body.statement: If \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_r\) are mutually independent real random variables and every \(Z_i\) is nonconstant, where \(r\ge1\), then \(\sum_{i=1}^r Z_i\) is nonconstant.
body.proof_tex: Suppose instead that \(\sum_i Z_i=c\) almost surely.  For each \(i\), the variable \(Z_i=c-\sum_{h\ne i}Z_h\) is measurable both with respect to \(\sigma(Z_i)\) and with respect to \(\sigma(Z_h:h\ne i)\).  These two sigma fields are independent.  Hence, for every Borel set \(A\), the event \(\{Z_i\in A\}\) is independent of itself and has probability zero or one.  Applying this to the half-lines with rational endpoints shows that the distribution function of \(Z_i\) takes only the values zero and one; monotonicity and right continuity then imply that it is the distribution function of a point mass.  Thus every \(Z_i\) is constant, contradicting the hypothesis.
